cause: The assembly's sworn decision to wipe out humankind
aftermath: Ziusudra granted eternal life; settled in Dilmun

vessel: A roofed reed boat sealed with pitch
aftermath: The gods regret it; Enlil institutes mortality and birth controls

cause: The gods' decision to destroy humankind
vessel: A seven-decked cube-shaped boat sealed with pitch
birds_released: Dove, swallow, raven (the raven does not return)
aftermath: Sacrifice; the gods gather “like flies”; Utnapishtim and wife granted immortality

cause: The wickedness of humankind; “the earth was filled with violence”
vessel: A gopher-wood ark, three decks, pitched inside and out
birds_released: A raven, then a dove released three times
aftermath: Burnt offering; the rainbow covenant never to flood the earth again

warned_by: Allah (Nuh preaches; the ark built under revelation)
cause: The people's persistent rejection of Nuh's warning
vessel: The ark, built “under Our eyes and Our inspiration”
aftermath: The disbelievers drown, including Nuh's own son; “O earth, swallow up thy water”

cause: Zeus's resolve to destroy the men of the Bronze Age
aftermath: Repopulation by casting stones — “the bones of their mother” — over the shoulder

vessel: An enormous boat (five stadia by two)
birds_released: Birds released three times (return; return muddied; do not return)
aftermath: Xisuthros, wife, daughter and pilot translated to dwell with the gods

vessel: A boat tied to the fish's horn
landing_place: The northern mountain (the “descent of the north”)
aftermath: Manu, sole survivor, generates humankind again through Iḍā

cause: The end of the Fourth Sun (Nahui-Atl, ‘4-Water’); the age destroyed by flood
aftermath: They roast the drowned people (now fish); the smoke angers the star-gods, and Tezcatlipoca turns Tata and Nena into dogs

source_text: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas; Molina, Relación de las fábulas y ritos de los Incas
survivor: A man and a woman sealed in a box
cause: Viracocha destroys the first race (a race of giants) for disobedience
aftermath: Viracocha refashions humanity from stone at Tiwanaku and repopulates the earth

approx_date: c. 1220 CE (Prose Edda); older eddic verse
cause: The blood of the slain primordial giant Ymir floods the world, drowning the frost giants
vessel: A lúðr (a hollowed tree-trunk), on Snorri's reading
aftermath: Bergelmir and his wife survive to continue the race of frost giants (jötnar)
